newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BHP says copper costs falling.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BHP says copper costs falling.

text.p: Costs at the Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd's (BHP) copper operations, BHP Copper, had fallen in the last three or four months, BHP chief executive officer John Prescott said on Sunday.
"We're seeing some reduction in our costs in the last three or four months, that's continuing," Prescott said in a television interview on Channel Nine's Sunday programme.

BHP reported a 32.2 percent fall in profits from its copper division to A$217 million in the six months to November 30, 1996. BHP Copper had a difficult 1996 year with a falling metal price after it purchased Magma Copper for US$2.4 billion.

"There's some major adjustments to be made in a couple of areas but we have improved our costs to some extent and of course, we're also seeing the benefit of a slightly higher price than was the case in the first quarter of BHP's year which ended in August," Prescott said.
Prescott also said BHP would make a decision on its Newcastle steelworks within the next three months.
BHP has indicated it is prepared to close the 81-year-old Newcastle mill if need be.

Speculation about the closure of Newcastle, and with it the loss of thousands of jobs, has prompted a parliamentary inquiry into the future of Australia's steel industry -- virtually a synonym for BHP, which supplies 75 percent of the local market.

"There will continue to be some form of downsizing in respect of some aspects of our operations but overall I would expect the steel group to expand, maybe internationally more so than in Australia, but our position in Australia will certainly be consolidated," Prescott said.
However, Prescott said the changes ahead for the steel group would not be as difficult as those that were behind the group.
